newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randgold hits new yr low after UK listing.
newsitem.headline: Randgold hits new yr low after UK listing.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Randgold and Exploration Company Ltd fell to a new year low on Friday following a lower-than-expected listing price of its exploration arm Randgold Resources on the London stock exchange, dealers said.
By about 1120 GMT Randgold's stock was unchanged from Thursday's close at 23.00 rand with 112,000 shares worth around 2.55 million rand exchanging hands.
The stock had earlier sank to a new year low of 22.50 rand.
"I think this (fall) could still be related to be listing price they had in London. The price was lower than what the market expected it to be," one Johannesburg Stock Exchange dealer said.

Randgold Resources' offer had been set at $16.50 per share -- lower than the $18 to $23 range expected originally by Randgold chairman Peter Flack on the exploration unit's debut on the London bourse on Thursday.
The size of the offer was also down at five million shares -- instead of the expected seven million.
Randgold Resources chief executive Mark Bristow conceded on Thursday that the price and the size of the offer did not meet the ambitious targets the company had set for itself.

He said gold's downturn to below $340 an ounce, the continuing impact on investors of the Bre-X scandal, where a Canadian junior exploration firm vastly overstated the potential of a gold find in Indonesia, and the general state of the major capital markets, continued to spook investor confidence in the mining exploration sector.
He added that the listing in itself was satisfactory considerting the "adverse circumstances which had developed since it had embarked on this exercise".
